newsitem.title: MEXICO: Apasco says 1996 Mexico cement demand up 2-4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Apasco says 1996 Mexico cement demand up 2-4 pct.

text.p: Cement makers Apasco estimates that demand for grey cement in Mexico will hit more than 22 million tonnes in 1996, according to a company report obtained by Reuters.
Compared to grey cement sales of 21.6 million tonnes in 1995, Apasco estimates demand for grey cement this year will grow "between two to four percent."
The company expects a slight recovery in grey cement sales after a disastrous 1995, during which sales slumped 23 percent compared to 1994 due to the severe economic recession.
Apasco forecast growth of "eight to ten percent" in domestic demand for ready-mixed concrete, which would then top six million tonnes during the year.
Apasco, a subsidiary of Swiss firm Holderbank, is Mexico's second largest cement firm, with about 25 percent market share and an installed annual capacity of 8.8 million metric tonnes.
